comment: What this platform contributes to a DeepSeek Harness profile, in one place
a machine can read. Three things use it: the profile bundles under
profile/ are assembled from these rows, an agent answers 'what can this
platform do' from it instead of guessing tool names, and a reader stops
having to find the four packages by reading a README table.
kind is the extension point a package attaches to, not the business domain
it serves. provenance says who supplies it and therefore where its source
lives: a builtin package ships with the product from this directory, a
workspace package is formed during use and lives in the user's workspace,
a third-party package arrives from a registry. status distinguishes what
runs today from what has a reserved place.

kinds.view: Registers ctx.documentPreviews and a slot body. Needs a browser half.
kinds.tool: Registers ctx.tools. Host only, so it loads in headless, sdk and acp.
kinds.chrome: Occupies a single-occupancy slot such as the sidebar brand.
kinds.profile: A composition-only bundle: rows and configuration, no code.
kinds.service: A long-lived platform service other packages call, rather than a tool the model invokes directly.
kinds.workflow: A domain workflow: inputs, step dependencies, acceptance rules and what it delivers.
kinds.skill-pack: Knowledge, not a plugin. Lives in the workspace under .dsh/skills and is found by the Harness itself.

packages.name: @deepseek-ai/iam-views
packages.note: One package, both domains: host/domains.ts is the table, and config.domains on the bundle row trims it to a subset.

packages.name: @deepseek-ai/iam-render
packages.note: ONE tool, iam_render_document: the platform's own headless renderer (IamNativeHeadlessMining) as a verb. Host only and no page, so a batch that writes the figures for a report runs in headless/sdk/acp like any other tool. The renderer's optional flags are probed from --help rather than assumed, so this package works against an older build: what the build does not support is named in the result's skipped[] instead of failing the render. The PPM is converted to PNG in-process and removed; a good frame with a bad teardown exit code is still a frame, with the exit code reported beside it.

packages.name: @deepseek-ai/iam-algorithm-bridge
packages.note: The retrieval surface and the execution entry for the algorithm library. Retrieval is two tools rather than one per catalog entry, so the catalog -- whatever size it grows to -- costs the prompt a constant. The execution entry is a Python half the host half spawns; a generated program runs as a grandchild so that a crash costs a tool call and not the session. `iam_algorithm_invoke` was planned and is NOT here: the catalog is invoked from inside a program, which is what the program runner is for.

packages.name: @deepseek-ai/iam-capability-forge
packages.note: The workshop, not a runner: capability_candidates finds recent successful runs worth proposing for freezing, capability_scaffold generates a package from templates, capability_validate checks the contract one finding per rule, capability_freeze calls the AlgorithmBridge's own freeze and records a lock, and capability_audit compares programs, locks, artifacts and figures. Frozen capabilities carry selectable step ids: a later iam_workflow_run can pass steps/resume to run only the steps it needs, and a missing prerequisite is refused rather than silently re-run. The plugin deliberately has no way to execute a capability; execution is iam_workflow_run. A capability is a directory of data, not an npm package, so the second capability costs no install.

packages.name: @deepseek-ai/iam-app-publisher
packages.note: The distribution door beside the forge. iam_app_publish copies one base executable (IamMining by default, IamDrawing on request), its DLLs, the selected frozen workflows, bridge.py, the vendored bindings, a portable Python runtime and an iam-app.json ribbon descriptor into one folder: publishing is a file copy, not a build, and the second app is the same call with another selection. Only active workflows ship; a draft or a dialog the manifest cannot drive is a refusal. The published app runs its workflows through bridge.py directly, so it needs no Harness installation and no model endpoint. `out` is confined to the session workspace, and the workspace root, .git, .iax and .agents are never replaceable. Paths come from the same IAM_* environment the packaged Desktop sets, so an installed app publishes without extra configuration. The same publisher is the `dsh app publish` command, so an operator and the agent publish the same bytes.

packages.name: @deepseek-ai/iam-mining-repository
packages.note: Reading, showing and CHANGING a Mining project. iam_mining_show resolves the elements a caller names and hands them to whichever carrier can draw them -- the sidebar panel for a portable .iam (the view is told what to show, so the document is opened and nothing is copied), or the native editor on the desktop for a columnar .iamh, which the browser build cannot read at all. The other four are the write door, and its whole shape is one rule: an edit does not publish. iam_mine_edit takes a declarative put/attach/erase description and iam_mine_verb runs a run(port) verb -- neither changes the mine, both write a .iaxd delta document; iam_mine_document reads one back in full, naming every resource it replaces and removes and needing no project to do it; and iam_mine_apply publishes one as the next revision, in place, revision-checked against the state the document was written from. It is a tool rather than the service the directory was reserved for, because the model is the one who has to be able to ask for an edit; the service face is what to add when a second package needs to call it. iam_mine_verb runs code the session wrote and therefore requires a configured programRunner; iam_mine_edit runs only this package's own verb and does not.

packages.name: @deepseek-ai/iam-artifact-store
packages.note: Candidate and final deliverables, so a computation's result can be reviewed before it becomes a revision.
